title: Netflix Has Peaked
content_html:
Netflix Has Peaked

Andrew Sharp, writing at Sharp Text last month after Netflix’s earnings, asking “Is Netflix Washed Now?”:

I offer this observation as a swirl of heightened anxiety surrounds the company, so let me clarify one thing up front: I’m not predicting imminent doom. Netflix content reaches a staggering 85% of American viewers and has 325 million subscribers globally. Growth is slowing, but that’s the law of large numbers. If practically everyone in America and much of the world is already subscribed to some version of Netflix, and churn rates are still low, then any concern is relative. Going forward: cable is still dying, and even if the biggest premium distribution platform in the world can’t make great content of its own, it can still license movies, TV and sports rights. Netflix can then spread those costs across hundreds of millions of subscribers and a steadily growing ads business, seeing more engagement in a week than Apple TV sees in a year.

So no, the company’s not doomed today or destined for collapse tomorrow. Instead, I think what’s interesting to consider is that Netflix has almost certainly peaked. As a cultural force, as a business success story, and as an entertainment death star destined to swallow Hollywood whole, the arrows are all pointing the wrong direction.

Sometimes the problem with a company isn’t that it isn’t a good business, but merely that it isn’t as good a business as it holds itself up to be. A billion-dollar business ought to be a good thing, but it’s a disaster if the company is valued by investors as a trillion-dollar business. That’s Netflix.

To me it’s backwards that Netflix is valued at $300 billion, roughly the 50th most valued company in the world, and Disney is valued at $180 billion, roughly 120th. Netflix has a streaming video service and owns some IP, like Stranger Things and Squid Game. Disney owns two streaming video services (Disney+ and Hulu), and owns some IP. Little stuff like Mickey Mouse, Star Wars, Marvel, the Disney princesses, and everything from Pixar. Netflix has started dabbling in sports; Disney owns ESPN. Disney owns the world’s biggest and best theme parks and an entire cruise ship line.

It’s true that Netflix’s streaming service is by far the biggest in the world, and likely will remain so for the foreseeable future. But Disney+ combined with Hulu is clearly in second place globally.

For the most recent 12 months:

DisneyNetflix
Revenue$97 B$48 B
Net Profit$11 B$14 B
Net Margin11.5%28%

Netflix is generating slightly more profit on half the revenue. With its theme parks, resorts, and cruise ships, big parts of Disney are effectively hardware, not software — so it’s almost inevitable its margins will be lower than a pure software play like Netflix. But those “hardware” businesses diversify Disney. How confident are you that Netflix will remain the undisputed leader in streaming 10 years from now, or 25? I’d bet good money that Walt Disney World will be the world’s biggest, best, and most profitable theme park 50 years from now. And it’s a joke to compare the value and longevity of the two companies’ IP.

I don’t know that Disney is undervalued by the market, but I sure think Netflix is overvalued. And as for quality, I’ve watched a bit more Netflix original content this summer than I had of late. David Attenborough’s A Gorilla Story was a splendid documentary, but nature documentaries don’t pay the bills. A few other things I watched (or at least watched part of) were absolute dreck. Not high-quality fun trash like Tiger King but amateur-hour I’m-worried-I-lost-a-few-IQ-points-by-watching-it trash. We pay $27/month for Netflix premium and I can say unequivocally that it’s not worth it. I continue paying for it because I’m willing to overpay for it the same way I am for beverages at a hotel — it’s money I’m willing to squander, knowing full well I’m squandering it.

It feels to me like Mr. Market is getting increasingly skeptical whether Netflix justifies its valuation, and Netflix is getting a little squirrelly and desperate trying to come up with an answer. Simple question: what’s their moat? It sure isn’t content quality.

★ Tuesday, 11 August 2026

sentences.zh: 比较两家公司知识产权的价值和寿命简直就是一个笑话。

sentences.zh: 至于质量，今年夏天我观看的 Netflix 原创内容比最近多了一些。

sentences.en: David Attenborough’s A Gorilla Story was a splendid documentary, but nature documentaries don’t pay the bills.
sentences.zh: 大卫·阿滕伯勒的《大猩猩的故事》是一部精彩的纪录片，但自然纪录片却无法赚钱。

sentences.en: A few other things I watched (or at least watched part of) were absolute dreck.
sentences.zh: 我看过的其他一些东西（或者至少看了一部分）绝对是垃圾。

sentences.zh: 不是像《虎王》那样的高质量有趣的垃圾，而是业余时间我担心看它会失去一些智商点的垃圾。

sentences.zh: 我们每月为 Netflix 付费服务支付 27 美元，我可以明确地说，这不值得。

sentences.zh: 我继续付钱是因为我愿意为它多付钱，就像我在酒店买饮料一样——我愿意挥霍这些钱，我清楚地知道我正在挥霍它。

sentences.en: It feels to me like Mr. Market is getting increasingly skeptical whether Netflix justifies its valuation, and Netflix is getting a little squirrelly and desperate trying to come up with an answer.

sentences.zh: 简单的问题：他们的护城河是什么？

sentences.en: Going forward: cable is still dying, and even if the biggest premium distribution platform in the world can’t make great content of its own, it can still license movies, TV and sports rights.
sentences.zh: 展望未来：有线电视仍在消亡，即使世界上最大的优质发行平台无法制作自己的精彩内容，它仍然可以授权电影、电视和体育赛事的转播权。

sentences.en: Netflix can then spread those costs across hundreds of millions of subscribers and a steadily growing ads business, seeing more engagement in a week than Apple TV sees in a year.
sentences.zh: 然后，Netflix 可以将这些成本分摊到数亿订阅用户和稳步增长的广告业务上，一周内的参与度就比 Apple TV 一年内的参与度还要高。

blocks.html_en: So no, the company’s not doomed today or destined for collapse tomorrow. Instead, I think what’s interesting to consider is that Netflix has almost certainly peaked. As a cultural force, as a business success story, and as an entertainment death star destined to swallow Hollywood whole, the arrows are all pointing the wrong direction.

sentences.en: So no, the company’s not doomed today or destined for collapse tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 所以不，该公司今天并没有注定要失败，明天也不会注定崩溃。

sentences.en: Instead, I think what’s interesting to consider is that Netflix has almost certainly peaked.
sentences.zh: 相反，我认为有趣的是，Netflix 几乎肯定已经达到顶峰。

sentences.en: As a cultural force, as a business success story, and as an entertainment death star destined to swallow Hollywood whole, the arrows are all pointing the wrong direction.
sentences.zh: 作为一种文化力量，作为一个商业成功故事，作为一个注定要吞噬整个好莱坞的娱乐死星，箭头都指向了错误的方向。

blocks.html_en: Sometimes the problem with a company isn’t that it isn’t a good business, but merely that it isn’t as good a business as it holds itself up to be. A billion-dollar business ought to be a good thing, but it’s a disaster if the company is valued by investors as a trillion-dollar business. That’s Netflix.

sentences.en: Sometimes the problem with a company isn’t that it isn’t a good business, but merely that it isn’t as good a business as it holds itself up to be.
sentences.zh: 有时，一家公司的问题并不在于它不是一家好企业，而只是它没有像它自称的那么好。

sentences.en: A billion-dollar business ought to be a good thing, but it’s a disaster if the company is valued by investors as a trillion-dollar business.
sentences.zh: 十亿美元的企业应该是一件好事，但如果公司被投资者评价为万亿美元的企业，那就是一场灾难。

sentences.en: That’s Netflix.
sentences.zh: 那是Netflix。

blocks.html_en: To me it’s backwards that Netflix is valued at $300 billion, roughly the 50th most valued company in the world, and Disney is valued at $180 billion, roughly 120th. Netflix has a streaming video service and owns some IP, like Stranger Things and Squid Game. Disney owns two streaming video services (Disney+ and Hulu), and owns some IP. Little stuff like Mickey Mouse, Star Wars, Marvel, the Disney princesses, and everything from Pixar. Netflix has started dabbling in sports; Disney owns ESPN. Disney owns the world’s biggest and best theme parks and an entire cruise ship line.

sentences.en: To me it’s backwards that Netflix is valued at $300 billion, roughly the 50th most valued company in the world, and Disney is valued at $180 billion, roughly 120th.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，Netflix 的估值为 3000 亿美元，大约在全球最有价值的公司中排名第 50 位，而迪士尼的估值为 1800 亿美元，大约排名第 120 位，这是倒退的。

sentences.en: Netflix has a streaming video service and owns some IP, like Stranger Things and Squid Game.
sentences.zh: Netflix拥有流媒体视频服务，并拥有一些IP，例如《怪奇物语》和《鱿鱼游戏》。

sentences.en: Disney owns two streaming video services (Disney+ and Hulu), and owns some IP.
sentences.zh: 迪士尼拥有两项流媒体视频服务（Disney+和Hulu），并拥有一些IP。

sentences.en: Little stuff like Mickey Mouse, Star Wars, Marvel, the Disney princesses, and everything from Pixar.
sentences.zh: 像米老鼠、星球大战、漫威、迪士尼公主以及皮克斯的一切小东西。

sentences.en: Netflix has started dabbling in sports; Disney owns ESPN.
sentences.zh: Netflix 开始涉足体育领域；迪士尼拥有 ESPN。

sentences.en: Disney owns the world’s biggest and best theme parks and an entire cruise ship line.
sentences.zh: 迪士尼拥有世界上最大、最好的主题公园和整个游轮航线。

blocks.html_en: It’s true that Netflix’s streaming service is by far the biggest in the world, and likely will remain so for the foreseeable future. But Disney+ combined with Hulu is clearly in second place globally.

sentences.en: It’s true that Netflix’s streaming service is by far the biggest in the world, and likely will remain so for the foreseeable future.
sentences.zh: 确实，Netflix 的流媒体服务是迄今为止世界上最大的，并且在可预见的未来很可能仍将如此。

sentences.en: But Disney+ combined with Hulu is clearly in second place globally.
sentences.zh: 但 Disney+ 与 Hulu 的结合显然在全球排名第二。

sentences.en: For the most recent 12 months:
sentences.zh: 最近 12 个月：

sentences.en: Disney
sentences.zh: 迪士尼

sentences.en: Netflix
Revenue
sentences.zh: 收入

sentences.en: Net Profit
sentences.zh: 纯利

sentences.en: Net Margin
sentences.zh: 净利润率

blocks.html_en: Netflix is generating slightly more profit on half the revenue. With its theme parks, resorts, and cruise ships, big parts of Disney are effectively hardware, not software — so it’s almost inevitable its margins will be lower than a pure software play like Netflix. But those “hardware” businesses diversify Disney. How confident are you that Netflix will remain the undisputed leader in streaming 10 years from now, or 25? I’d bet good money that Walt Disney World will be the world’s biggest, best, and most profitable theme park 50 years from now. And it’s a joke to compare the value and longevity of the two companies’ IP.

sentences.en: Netflix is generating slightly more profit on half the revenue.
sentences.zh: Netflix 的一半收入创造了略多的利润。

sentences.en: With its theme parks, resorts, and cruise ships, big parts of Disney are effectively hardware, not software — so it’s almost inevitable its margins will be lower than a pure software play like Netflix.
sentences.zh: 凭借主题公园、度假村和游轮，迪士尼的很大一部分实际上是硬件，而不是软件——因此它的利润率几乎不可避免地会低于 Netflix 这样的纯软件公司。

sentences.en: But those “hardware” businesses diversify Disney.
sentences.zh: 但这些“硬件”业务使迪士尼实现了多元化。

sentences.en: How confident are you that Netflix will remain the undisputed leader in streaming 10 years from now, or 25?
sentences.zh: 您对 Netflix 在 10 年后或 25 年后仍然是流媒体领域无可争议的领导者有多大信心？

sentences.en: I’d bet good money that Walt Disney World will be the world’s biggest, best, and most profitable theme park 50 years from now.
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌，50 年后，华特迪士尼世界将成为世界上最大、最好、最赚钱的主题公园。

sentences.en: And it’s a joke to compare the value and longevity of the two companies’ IP.
sentences.zh: 比较两家公司知识产权的价值和寿命简直就是一个笑话。

blocks.html_en: I don’t know that Disney is undervalued by the market, but I sure think Netflix is overvalued. And as for quality, I’ve watched a bit more Netflix original content this summer than I had of late. David Attenborough’s A Gorilla Story was a splendid documentary, but nature documentaries don’t pay the bills. A few other things I watched (or at least watched part of) were absolute dreck. Not high-quality fun trash like Tiger King but amateur-hour I’m-worried-I-lost-a-few-IQ-points-by-watching-it trash. We pay $27/month for Netflix premium and I can say unequivocally that it’s not worth it. I continue paying for it because I’m willing to overpay for it the same way I am for beverages at a hotel — it’s money I’m willing to squander, knowing full well I’m squandering it.

sentences.en: I don’t know that Disney is undervalued by the market, but I sure think Netflix is overvalued.
sentences.zh: 我不知道迪士尼是否被市场低估，但我确信Netflix被高估了。

sentences.en: And as for quality, I’ve watched a bit more Netflix original content this summer than I had of late.
sentences.zh: 至于质量，今年夏天我观看的 Netflix 原创内容比最近多了一些。

sentences.en: David Attenborough’s A Gorilla Story was a splendid documentary, but nature documentaries don’t pay the bills.
sentences.zh: 大卫·阿滕伯勒的《大猩猩的故事》是一部精彩的纪录片，但自然纪录片却无法赚钱。

sentences.en: A few other things I watched (or at least watched part of) were absolute dreck.
sentences.zh: 我看过的其他一些东西（或者至少看了一部分）绝对是垃圾。

sentences.en: Not high-quality fun trash like Tiger King but amateur-hour I’m-worried-I-lost-a-few-IQ-points-by-watching-it trash.
sentences.zh: 不是像《虎王》那样的高质量有趣的垃圾，而是业余时间我担心看它会失去一些智商点的垃圾。

sentences.en: We pay $27/month for Netflix premium and I can say unequivocally that it’s not worth it.
sentences.zh: 我们每月为 Netflix 付费服务支付 27 美元，我可以明确地说，这不值得。

sentences.en: I continue paying for it because I’m willing to overpay for it the same way I am for beverages at a hotel — it’s money I’m willing to squander, knowing full well I’m squandering it.
sentences.zh: 我继续付钱是因为我愿意为它多付钱，就像我在酒店买饮料一样——我愿意挥霍这些钱，我清楚地知道我正在挥霍它。

blocks.html_en: It feels to me like Mr. Market is getting increasingly skeptical whether Netflix justifies its valuation, and Netflix is getting a little squirrelly and desperate trying to come up with an answer. Simple question: what’s their moat? It sure isn’t content quality.

sentences.en: It feels to me like Mr. Market is getting increasingly skeptical whether Netflix justifies its valuation, and Netflix is getting a little squirrelly and desperate trying to come up with an answer.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，市场先生越来越怀疑 Netflix 的估值是否合理，而 Netflix 在试图给出答案时也变得有点古怪和绝望。

sentences.en: Simple question: what’s their moat?
sentences.zh: 简单的问题：他们的护城河是什么？

sentences.en: It sure isn’t content quality.
sentences.zh: 这肯定不是内容质量。

content_html_zh:
Netflix 已经达到顶峰
安德鲁·夏普 (Andrew Sharp) 上个月在 Netflix 公布财报后在 Sharp Text 撰文，问道“Netflix 现在被洗劫了吗？”：我提出这一观察是因为公司周围的焦虑加剧，所以让我先澄清一件事：我并不是在预测即将到来的厄运。 Netflix 的内容覆盖了高达 85% 的美国观众，在全球拥有 3.25 亿订阅者。 增长正在放缓，但这就是大数定律。 如果几乎美国和世界大部分地区的每个人都已经订阅了 Netflix 的某个版本，并且流失率仍然很低，那么任何担忧都是相对的。 展望未来：有线电视仍在消亡，即使世界上最大的优质发行平台无法制作自己的精彩内容，它仍然可以授权电影、电视和体育赛事的转播权。 然后，Netflix 可以将这些成本分摊到数亿订阅用户和稳步增长的广告业务上，一周内的参与度就比 Apple TV 一年内的参与度还要高。 所以不，该公司今天并没有注定要失败，明天也不会注定崩溃。 相反，我认为有趣的是，Netflix 几乎肯定已经达到顶峰。 作为一种文化力量，作为一个商业成功故事，作为一个注定要吞噬整个好莱坞的娱乐死星，箭头都指向了错误的方向。 有时，一家公司的问题并不在于它不是一家好企业，而只是它没有像它自称的那么好。 十亿美元的企业应该是一件好事，但如果公司被投资者评价为万亿美元的企业，那就是一场灾难。 那是Netflix。 对我来说，Netflix 的估值为 3000 亿美元，大约在全球最有价值的公司中排名第 50 位，而迪士尼的估值为 1800 亿美元，大约排名第 120 位，这是倒退的。 Netflix拥有流媒体视频服务，并拥有一些IP，例如《怪奇物语》和《鱿鱼游戏》。 迪士尼拥有两项流媒体视频服务（Disney+和Hulu），并拥有一些IP。 像米老鼠、星球大战、漫威、迪士尼公主以及皮克斯的一切小东西。 Netflix 开始涉足体育领域；迪士尼拥有 ESPN。 迪士尼拥有世界上最大、最好的主题公园和整个游轮航线。 确实，Netflix 的流媒体服务是迄今为止世界上最大的，并且在可预见的未来很可能仍将如此。 但 Disney+ 与 Hulu 的结合显然在全球排名第二。 最近 12 个月：迪士尼 Netflix 收入 $97 B$48 B 净利润 $11 B$14 B 净利润 11.5%28% Netflix 的一半收入略多于利润。 凭借主题公园、度假村和游轮，迪士尼的很大一部分实际上是硬件，而不是软件——因此它的利润率几乎不可避免地会低于 Netflix 这样的纯软件公司。 但这些“硬件”业务使迪士尼实现了多元化。 您对 Netflix 在 10 年后或 25 年后仍然是流媒体领域无可争议的领导者有多大信心？ 我敢打赌，50 年后，华特迪士尼世界将成为世界上最大、最好、最赚钱的主题公园。 比较两家公司知识产权的价值和寿命简直就是一个笑话。 我不知道迪士尼是否被市场低估，但我确信Netflix被高估了。 至于质量，今年夏天我观看的 Netflix 原创内容比最近多了一些。 大卫·阿滕伯勒的《大猩猩的故事》是一部精彩的纪录片，但自然纪录片却无法赚钱。 我看过的其他一些东西（或者至少看了一部分）绝对是垃圾。 不是像《虎王》那样的高质量有趣的垃圾，而是业余时间我担心看它会失去一些智商点的垃圾。 我们每月为 Netflix 付费服务支付 27 美元，我可以明确地说，这不值得。 我继续付钱是因为我愿意为它多付钱，就像我在酒店买饮料一样——我愿意挥霍这些钱，我清楚地知道我正在挥霍它。 在我看来，市场先生越来越怀疑 Netflix 的估值是否合理，而 Netflix 在试图给出答案时也变得有点古怪和绝望。 简单的问题：他们的护城河是什么？ 这肯定不是内容质量。 ★ 2026 年 8 月 11 日，星期二
